quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #14
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 18

questions.question: Which statement about drugs and driving is true?

options.text: Any prescription drug is safe to use if you don't feel drowsy.
Over-the-counter drugs can affect your driving ability.
Only illegal drugs can affect your driving ability.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over-the-counter drugs can affect your driving ability.
questions.explanation: Prescription and over-the-counter drugs can affect your ability to drive. This includes drugs for colds, allergies, and other conditions. It is illegal to drive while under the influence of any drug that affects your driving ability. The law applies to all drugs — illegal, prescription, and over-the-counter.

questions.question: You are driving on a narrow road when you meet an oncoming vehicle. You must:

options.text: Pull completely off the road and stop.
Give the oncoming vehicle at least half of the road.
Tell the other vehicle to pull over.
Turn on your high beams so the other driver sees you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the oncoming vehicle at least half of the road.
questions.explanation: On narrow roads, give vehicles coming toward you at least half of the road. Both drivers need enough space to pass each other safely.

questions.question: An inattentive driver is someone who:

options.text: Looks away from the road or daydreams while driving.
Looks at a passenger while having a conversation.
Only watches the car in front of them.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Avoid distractions like looking at passengers, searching for items, reading, sightseeing, or daydreaming while driving. Keep your attention on the road by checking your mirrors and instrument panel regularly. These safe habits help you stay focused as a driver.

questions.question: Strong wind gusts on highways:

options.text: Generally affect only large vehicles.
Only cause visibility problems.
Can affect all types of vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can affect all types of vehicles.
questions.explanation: Strong wind affects all drivers, not just large vehicles. Wind lowers visibility by blowing dust and dirt onto the road. It can also physically push a vehicle.

questions.question: During an emergency roadside stop, you do not need to use your parking brake.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: Always use your parking brake during an emergency roadside stop. Turn on your emergency flashers to warn other drivers.

questions.question: To help prevent crashes, you should:

options.text: Let other drivers know what you are doing.
Ignore other drivers on the road.
Drive only on side streets and back roads.
Avoid driving during rush hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let other drivers know what you are doing.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers do something others don't expect. Communicate with other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians by signaling before slowing down, stopping, or turning. Use your emergency signals or horn when needed.

questions.question: On long trips, you can prevent drowsiness by:

options.text: Turning on your car radio.
Slowing down.
Stopping to rest at regular times.
Moving your eyes from side to side as you drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stopping to rest at regular times.
questions.explanation: To prevent drowsiness on long trips, stop regularly to rest and stretch. Do this even if you don't feel tired.

questions.question: If you parallel park facing downhill:

options.text: Turn your wheels toward the curb or edge.
Turn your wheels away from the curb or edge.
Keep your wheels straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels toward the curb or edge.
questions.explanation: When parking downhill, turn your wheels toward the curb. When parking uphill without a curb, turn your wheels toward the edge. When parking uphill with a curb, turn your wheels away from the curb.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle's right wheels leave the pavement?

options.text: Stop quickly.
Pull completely off the road and get back on when safe.
Speed up and steer back onto the road quickly.
Release the gas, slow down, and gently steer back onto the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the gas, slow down, and gently steer back onto the road.
questions.explanation: If your right wheels leave the pavement, stay calm. Release the gas pedal and steer the vehicle parallel to the road. Slow down and ease back onto the road by keeping both hands on the wheel and making a small turn. Check for traffic before steering back onto the pavement.

questions.question: In fog or mist, do not use your high beam headlights because:

options.text: The light reflects back into your eyes.
Oncoming vehicles might not see you.
Vehicles behind you may follow too closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: The light reflects back into your eyes.
questions.explanation: In fog or mist, do not use high beam headlights. The light bounces back toward you, making it harder to see.

questions.question: You do not have to stop for a school bus with red flashing lights if it is on a private road.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: You must stop for a school bus with red flashing lights and a stop arm extended. This rule applies on both public and private roads.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: No right turn.
Drive only in the direction of the arrow.
Curve ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive only in the direction of the arrow.
questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign. It tells drivers they must drive in the direction shown by the arrow.

questions.question: You are approaching an intersection with a steady yellow traffic light. If you have not entered the intersection yet, you should:

options.text: Speed up to beat the red light.
Reduce your speed and proceed carefully through the intersection.
Come to a safe stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a safe stop.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means prepare to stop. If you are already in the intersection, clear it quickly and safely.

questions.question: When dealing with pedestrians, a driver must:

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian sees your vehicle.
Always yield the right-of-way, even if the pedestrian is in the wrong.
Yield the right-of-way only when the pedestrian has the legal right to cross.
Slow down and honk near a crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always yield the right-of-way, even if the pedestrian is in the wrong.
questions.explanation: You must do everything possible to avoid hitting a pedestrian or another vehicle, no matter what. Always yield to pedestrians, even if they are crossing where they should not be.

questions.question: An octagonal sign is always a:

options.text: Speed limit sign.
Stop sign.
Hospital sign.
Railroad warning sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop sign.
questions.explanation: All octagonal signs are stop signs. Come to a complete stop at every red, eight-sided sign.

questions.question: Which statement is true about changing lanes?

options.text: You only need to turn and look over your right shoulder for any lane change.
Look over your right shoulder for a right lane change and your left shoulder for a left lane change.
Vehicles with two outside mirrors have no blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your right shoulder for a right lane change and your left shoulder for a left lane change.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, signal and check all mirrors. Look over your shoulder to see your blind spot. Make sure no vehicle, motorcycle, or bicycle is in the next lane.

questions.question: Large vehicles have blind spots that can extend up to 200 feet directly behind them.

options.text: TRUE
FALSE

questions.correctAnswerText: TRUE
questions.explanation: Large vehicles have blind spots extending up to 200 feet behind them. Do not tailgate large vehicles because the driver cannot see you.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Falling rocks
Trucks use second gear
Steep hill

questions.correctAnswerText: Steep hill
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. This sign means a steep hill is ahead. Slow down and shift to a lower gear to control your speed and protect your brakes.

questions.question: Before passing another vehicle, you should signal:

options.text: Just before changing lanes.
At any time.
After changing lanes.
Early enough for others to know your plans.

questions.correctAnswerText: Early enough for others to know your plans.
questions.explanation: Signal early before passing so other drivers know what you are about to do.

questions.question: A broken yellow line down the center of a road means:

options.text: A construction zone is ahead.
Passing is not permitted from either direction.
Passing is permitted from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is permitted from either direction.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line separates traffic on a two-lane road. Any driver may pass when there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: Can you stop in a travel lane to let out a passenger?

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: Never stop in a travel lane for any reason. This includes letting out passengers, confusion, or breakdowns. Keep moving until you can safely pull off the road.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: A steep hill is ahead.
You must turn left ahead.
Do not enter.
A four-way intersection is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A four-way intersection is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a four-way intersection is coming.

questions.question: When an emergency vehicle with sirens and flashing lights approaches, should you pull to the right and wait for it to pass?

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle uses its lights and sirens, you must pull to the right side of the road right away and let it pass.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you never do?

options.text: Change lanes inside an intersection.
Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.
Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes inside an intersection.
questions.explanation: Never change lanes inside an intersection. Always look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes. Watch for other drivers moving into the same lane.

questions.question: What does a flashing red traffic light mean?

options.text: The same as a yield sign.
The light is about to turn green.
The same as a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same as a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means you must stop completely, yield to traffic and pedestrians, and go only when it is safe. This is the same as a stop sign.
